evidence_items.locator: paragraphs 6-7, quoting GitHub CPO Mario Rodriguez

receipt.public_excerpt: "GitHub has absorbed much of the escalating inference cost behind that usage, but the current premium request model is no longer sustainable."

evidence_items.explanation: GitHub's product chief says GitHub absorbed rising inference costs under fixed-price Copilot plans. That is Microsoft subsidizing compute beyond what subscriptions charged. The quote describes the state before the April 2026 change.

receipt.public_excerpt: “One user consumed tens of thousands in model usage on a $200 plan,” the company noted.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic itself said a $200-a-month subscriber used model usage worth tens of thousands of dollars, far more than the plan price.

receipt.public_excerpt: "Insane thing: We are currently losing money on OpenAI Pro subscriptions!" he wrote in a post.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's CEO said the $200 Pro subscription lost money because people used it more than expected, so usage cost more than the price.

receipt.public_excerpt: the company has reached positive gross margins on its sales to large enterprises, but continues to lose money on individual developer accounts, according to one person.

evidence_items.explanation: Anonymous-source report that Cursor still lost money on individual subscribers just before the post, after earlier negative gross margins overall.

receipt.public_excerpt: If a heavy Claude Code Max user consumes $5,000 worth of tokens at Anthropic's retail API prices, and the actual compute cost is roughly 10% of that, Anthropic is looking at approximately $500 in real compute cost for the heaviest users.

evidence_items.explanation: Disputes how large Anthropic's subsidy is, arguing actual serving cost is about 10% of list price. Even so, it estimates a loss of about $300 a month on the heaviest users, so it weakens the size of the subsidy, not its existence.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Why did we change the plan?'

receipt.public_excerpt: Though most users’ costs have stayed fairly constant, the hardest requests cost an order of magnitude more than simple ones. API-based pricing is the best way to reflect that.

evidence_items.explanation: Cursor explains that flat request pricing let hard requests cost far more than they were charged, which is why it moved Pro to usage-based pricing in mid-2025.

unresolved_gaps: 'Every other AI company' cannot be checked across all firms; only the four named companies were tested.
GitHub's own blog page did not return the post body, so GitHub's statement is cited through ITPro's quotation.
No named company published per-user serving costs. How large the subsidy was in actual compute cost, rather than list price, remains disputed (e5).
The Cursor evidence rests on anonymous sources.
